headline: Majors underwater against 200s, but momentum codes positive while whales withdraw coins; positioning is long and expensive across the board.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit below their 200-day simple moving averages, and none has triggered a golden cross. This is a bear-regime market by the structural measure: Bitcoin at 64,813 is 48 percent off its 12-month high of 82,018; Ethereum at 1,942 is down 59.7 percent from 2,370; Solana has fallen 69.5 percent to 75.58; Cardano is the furthest underwater at minus 83.5 percent. The broader frame corroborates the picture: total market cap sits at 2.3 trillion and fell 0.11 percent over the last 24 hours. Bitcoin dominance is firm at 56.5 percent, a sign that when capital does move, it gravitates toward the safest asset. Nothing here suggests a market in recovery; this is a regime that has held for enough time to matter.

Against that backdrop, the momentum picture shows an internal contradiction worth noting. Bitcoin's RSI-14 reads 52.9, neutral territory, but its MACD sits above the signal line: positive momentum without much conviction. Ethereum is more bullish on the technicals, RSI at 62.7 with MACD above signal, and it printed a three-day gain of 3.65 percent, strongest among the tier-one names. Solano, however, breaks the pattern: RSI at 48.4, MACD below signal, and it fell 1.33 percent on the day. The smaller names show mixed signals as well. Cardano, which is down 83.5 percent from its peak, has both RSI and MACD in retreat, reading 41.9 and negative momentum. Doge shows MACD above signal but RSI at 42.6, typical of a name bouncing off oversold without real follow-through. The coherence is low: Ethereum's momentum looks freshest, but Bitcoin's is soft, and the majority of the field is either resting or declining. This is not a synchronized move; it is churn inside a downtrend.

Positioning on perpetuals reveals a market where leverage is tilted long and the cost of that bet is beginning to matter. Bitcoin's 8-hour funding rate sits at 0.51 percent, which annualizes to 5.5 percent, a meaningful cost for carry. Over 1.98 billion dollars in open interest sits at OKX alone, and the long-to-short ratio is 1.55 to one, meaning there is 55 percent more leverage on the bullish side. In the last 24 hours, 1,434 positions liquidated across both sides, with 1.02 million dollars in long liquidations versus 822 thousand in shorts: longs are washing out more, which is consistent with a long-crowded market meeting resistance. Ethereum's picture is similar but less expensive: funding at 0.09 percent annualized, open interest of 1.46 billion, and a 1.26 long-short ratio. Liquidations over the prior nine hours show 937 thousand longs flushed versus 534 thousand shorts. Solana stands apart: funding is negative at minus 0.47 percent eight-hourly, meaning shorts are paying longs to hold the bet. The long-short ratio is 2.56 to one, the most asymmetrically long of any name, and open interest is only 208 million. Negative funding should cool off longs over time, but the ratio suggests they are still confident. Doge is even more extreme, a 3.18 long-short ratio with 0.92 percent positive funding, and liquidations show 1.34 million in longs flushed versus only 190 thousand in shorts. These are overcrowded bets from a positioning view: the long side is thick, the cost is rising, and washouts are already happening.

Whale flows over the last 72 hours tell a story of de-risking that contradicts some of the long bias on the derivatives side. Net Bitcoin movement off exchanges was 217.5 million dollars: 518 million withdrawn from exchanges versus 301 million deposited. The biggest single move was 320 million out of OKEx, followed by 116 million and then 81 million out of Kraken. Against this, whales moved 100.6 million dollars worth of USDT onto OKEx, a signal of dry powder staged and ready. The weekly trend is instructive: the prior four weeks show net flows of plus 1.33 billion, then minus 110 million, then plus 172 million, then plus 550 million. This week's net is negative in the shorter window (the 72-hour outflow), but the monthly backdrop is tilted to buying pressure. Stablecoin float overall sits at 306.2 billion and fell 1.39 percent over the last 30 days, a slow bleed that suggests capital is either being deployed or held in waiting. ETF flows for Bitcoin on July 24th came in at minus 240 million dollars, outflows on a single day, but the five-session net was positive at 33.9 million with the same direction only twice. ETH saw minus 70.7 million on the 24th but a five-session net of positive 103.8 million. Both are volatile on a day-to-day basis, but the multi-day aggregate is still ingesting traditional finance capital. Cumulative Bitcoin ETF inflows stand at 51.4 billion; cumulative Ethereum at 11.2 billion.

Sentiment is locked at fear, reading 30 on the gauge with a 30-day range of 11 to 33. The crowd is spooked, but not in panic territory. The tape, however, shows divergence: whales are selectively pulling Bitcoin off exchanges while staging stablecoin capital; leverage on Bitcoin and Ethereum is long, expensive, and leaking position; and momentum is mixed to soft, with only Ethereum showing real heat. The gap between what the crowd feels and what the money is doing is notable. Fear is present, but the big actors are hedging rather than fleeing, and spot ETF flows remain positive on a multi-day view. This is not capitulation; it is caution from experienced hands.

Watch for three conditions to signal a shift in this picture. First, a reversal in whale Bitcoin flows from off-exchange to on-exchange would suggest big holders are trimming stops or preparing to liquidate, a bearish tell. Second, a break above the 200-day moving average for Bitcoin or Ethereum would be the first structural crack in the regime, and a golden cross in either would confirm the start of recovery. Third, if the long-short ratio on Bitcoin drops below 1.3 to one or its funding flips negative, the long squeeze will have begun to reverse, and the oversized positioning will deflate. For now, the regime is down, positioning is crowded and expensive, and the big money is taking chips off the table. Momentum is a whisper, not a shout.
